text:
Can you write a cover letter for me? I'm 52 and I'm applying for an office manager job at a dental practice in my town. I've been out of work for 7 years caring for my mother, who died last spring.

My background:
- Before that I was office manager at a veterinary clinic for 11 years. It had 4 vets and 14 staff.
- I handled scheduling, billing, and the clinic's move from paper records to software in 2014.
- In my last three years there, unpaid invoices over 90 days went from about $38,000 to $9,000.
- During the 7 years at home I managed my mother's insurance claims and her appointments with 6 specialists.
- I haven't used Dentrix, which the posting lists. I used AVImark at the clinic.
- The practice has 3 dentists. The posting says the manager supervises 9 people.

Keep it under 300 words.

I left out your age because it doesn't belong in a cover letter. I kept the caregiving gap short and direct.

<final_document>
Dear [Hiring Manager's Name],

I am writing to apply for the Office Manager position at [Practice Name]. For eleven years I was office manager at [Clinic Name], a veterinary clinic with four veterinarians and fourteen staff. I would welcome the chance to bring that experience to a practice here in [Town].

At the clinic I handled scheduling and billing for a busy practice with several providers. In 2014 I led our move from paper records to practice management software, and I kept daily operations running while the staff adjusted to the new system. In my last three years there, I reduced invoices more than 90 days past due from about $38,000 to $9,000.

For the past seven years I stepped away from work to care for my mother full-time. I managed her insurance claims and coordinated her appointments with six specialists. That gave me a close view of medical billing and scheduling from the patient's side, and it showed me how much a well-run front office matters to the people it serves. My mother passed away this spring, and I am ready to return to the work I know.

I understand your practice uses Dentrix. My experience is with AVImark, but I have taken an entire office from paper to software once already, and I am confident I can learn Dentrix quickly.

I would be glad to talk about how I can support your dentists and your team. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]
[Phone] | [Email]
</final_document>

The letter is about 265 words. Some things to check before you send it:

- **Supervising staff:** You didn't say whether you directly supervised the 14 staff at the clinic. If you did, add a line such as "I supervised a staff of fourteen" to the second paragraph. The posting says this job manages 9 people, so that line would match it directly.
- **Dentrix:** If you can start a Dentrix tutorial or online course before you apply, change the Dentrix sentence to "I have already begun learning Dentrix." That's much stronger than a promise that you'll learn it.
- **Overdue invoices:** If you remember how you reduced the overdue invoices (for example, new payment policies or regular follow-up calls), adding a few words about it would make that result stronger.
